newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower on cash, mild forecast.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends lower on cash, mild forecast.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub gas futures ended near session lows Thursday as cash prices were dampened by mild weather moving across most of the U.S., sources said.
Six- to 10-day forecasts called for temperatures above- to much-above-normal throughout the eastern two-thirds of the U.S., with the most extreme temperatures likely on the East Coast next week.
After retreating to a low of $1.98 per mmBtu, March finished down 9.1 cents at $1.999. April remained stuck in the contango, settling down 6.1 cents at $1.991. Other months were also lower.

Also suppressing any rally in March in the near-term, traders said, is the upcoming three-day holiday weekend. NYMEX will suspend regular hours trading on Monday, Feb 17, in observance of the Presidents Day holiday.
Traders were pegging support in March at today's session low of $1.98 and then at $1.749. Resistance was seen in the $2.08-2.09 area, then at $2.25-2.30 and in the low-$2.50s.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast prices fell about 20 cents to the low-$2.20s. Midcontinent pipes were down about 25 cents to about $2.05, with Demarcation quoted around $2.15. At the New York city-gate, prices dropped into the $2.75-2.80 area, down at least 25 cents.
NYMEX said an estimated 49,523 Hub contracts traded, as compared with Wednesday's revised tally of 47,938. The 12-month strip dropped 4.5 cents to $2.061.
Although no contracts traded, March Permian settled 10 cents lower at $1.83, while March Alberta fell seven cents to $1.38.

On KCBT, March finished near session lows at $1.74, down 10.8 cents, while deferreds were four to six cents lower at the close. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 25.9 cents (NYMEX premium).
Pressuring the KCBT market early was talk of weaker cash prices in western Texas, where Permian deals were reported done in the low-$2 area.
